meta_description: Core-adjacent modernization on landing-zone discipline — release cadence from monthly to weekly and run-the-bank infrastructure cost down 27%

blocks.x: Core-adjacent modernization on landing-zone discipline — release cadence from monthly to weekly and run-the-bank infrastructure cost down 27%

Identity withheld — a US regional bank that had bought cloud twice and used it twice: two disconnected Landing Zones, release trains still monthly, and a data center renewal due in fourteen months. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline quarter measured delivery physics: 31 days median lead time from merge to production, and 62% of that time spent waiting on environment and control gates that existed on paper only.

Change advisory board packs were assembled by hand for every release. Evidence of control operation was gathered per release rather than produced continuously, so audit season froze delivery entirely.

We rebuilt delivery on a single landing zone with controls as code: identity, network and logging policy expressed once and inherited everywhere; evidence produced by the pipeline instead of gathered afterwards; and the CAB pack generated from the release record. The core stayed put — the value came from the 40 systems around it that had been holding delivery hostage.
